Why $80K of Dividends Pays $0 Federal Tax and a Salary Pays $9,243 (Canada)
The Dividend Tax Credit Explained With Real Numbers (2026)
yt.description:
$80,000 of income and $0 federal tax, legally. Here's the math (2026, federal, example).

Dana has no salary; her only income is $80,000 of eligible dividends from Canadian companies.
• Gross-up 38%: taxable on paper $110,400
• Federal tax after the basic personal amount: ≈ $16,525
• Dividend tax credit 15.0198% of $110,400: ≈ $16,582 → federal tax $0 (the credit is non-refundable)

The twist: the same $80,000 as a salary pays ≈ $9,243 of federal tax. The credit exists because the company already paid tax on its profits. Provinces have their own rates and credits.

Check what kind of income you earn: it changes the tax.

Next: OAS, and how to keep more of it.

Sources: canada.ca (CRA) line 40425; CRA T4127 (2026). Federal only, no other income. Example. General information, not advice.
